title: Create a repeatable monthly technical SEO check for zedu.chat, by Fri 4 Dec
description:
There is no single check that tells the team whether the basics are still in place after a release.

Success looks like: one script (plain curl and Python, no paid tools) and a one-page checklist that anyone on the team can run, covering robots.txt and sitemap.xml status, H1 count per page, title and description length, canonical tags, security headers, redirect hops for the http, www and trailing-slash variants, missing-page status codes and broken internal links. The first run's results are attached, and the document says plainly what the script cannot check.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: One Python script that reuses the checks other SEO goals already define, run after every release
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Several goals this week each define a check (robots/sitemap, one H1, title and description length, canonicals, security headers, soft 404s). One script that runs all of them gives the team a single pass/fail list. Tasks: (1) a standard-library-only Python script (urllib, html.parser) that takes the public URL list from the sitemap, or a fixed list until it exists, and prints a table per page plus the http/www/trailing-slash redirect hops and a made-up-URL status check; (2) a one-page checklist explaining each check and what 'fail' means; (3) run it on the live site, save the first report as the baseline, and add the command to the zedu-fe README or CI.

tasks.title: Deliver one repeatable Python SEO checker, checklist and current baseline

acceptedWorkstreams.title: One standard-library Python script with a baseline from today's live site
acceptedWorkstreams.description: A single Python script using only the standard library (urllib, re, csv), so anyone can run it without installing anything. It reads the page list from sitemap.xml when that exists, otherwise from a fixed list, and writes one CSV row per page: status, robots and sitemap content type, H1 count, title and description length, canonical, the five security headers, redirect hops for http, www and trailing-slash variants, missing-page status and broken internal links. Today's run would already flag known problems (home has 9 H1s, /solutions 0; robots.txt and sitemap.xml return HTML; no security headers), which proves the checks work. Tasks: script and one-page checklist (SEO), first run with a 'what this can't check' note (SEO).
